title: Mrs. Michal Tawil: Do we Really Need Tree of Opinion (Class # 30)

chapters.title: Introduction and the Sukkah story
chapters.about: Reflecting on holiday lights and the process of building a sukkah with her husband.

chapters.title: The avodah of Shiviti Hashem lenegdi tamid
chapters.about: Defining the concept of equality and seeing Hashem in front of us at all times.

chapters.title: Understanding the Etz Hadaat
chapters.about: Interpreting the tree of knowledge as a tree of opinion and the danger of judging others.

chapters.title: Clearing the mind for Daat Hashem
chapters.about: Moving away from constant internal commentary to allow God's knowledge to enter.

chapters.title: Faith in others and personal growth
chapters.about: Trusting that others have their own tafkid and focusing on one's own internal work.

chapters.title: Kavod and the importance of our desires
chapters.about: Respecting one's own desires and the story of the lounge chair.

chapters.title: Living across from Hashem
chapters.about: The difference between living for others' expectations versus living for one's own desires.

chapters.title: Asking what situations teach us about ourselves
chapters.about: Shifting focus from judging others to identifying one's own next level of growth.

summary: Mrs. Tawil discusses the avodah of Shiviti Hashem lenegdi tamid, focusing on how to maintain a relationship with Hashem by relinquishing personal opinions and judgments about others. She explains that the Etz Hadaat in Bereshit represents an 'opinion tree' that leads to death, and encourages listeners to instead clear their minds of constant commentary to allow Daat Hashem to enter. Through personal stories about her sukkah and family, she demonstrates how to stop living in other people's heads and instead focus on one's own desires and growth.
questions: How can I stop having opinions about everything that happens around me?
What does it mean to stand across from Hashem instead of across from other people?
How can I stop feeling guilty or needing to apologize for my personal choices?
Why does having an opinion about others lead to a feeling of death?
How do I use difficult situations to learn about my own growth?
